answer: When a traveller crosses a border, the handset roams onto a partner network and the handover leaves a signed trail across both carriers, like a raven flying between two rooftops and seen from both. The verifier asks both sides to confirm the same session, and a haven of forged roaming claims collapses when the foreign network has no record of the visit. A ripple of truth remains: only a physical device with a real roaming agreement can produce a two-sided trail, and a farm would need paid roaming deals in every country it pretends to visit.
